text:
Dylan Cozens has quietly found his scoring touch for Ottawa: six goals and 12 points in a 13-game stretch through Nov. 25, as Graeme Nichols of Coming Down the Pipe pointed out, including two in a loss to Philadelphia where the Senators blew a 5-2 lead. "It is frustrating not closing out a 5-2 game in the third," was his line to TSN that night.

The season total, 18 points in 27 games, still understates him. Ottawa has scored 5.8 fewer goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and his points per 60 minutes sit in the lower half of our talent range. His own finishing is about where it should be: seven goals on 8.0 expected.

The concern is elsewhere. Evolving-Hockey rated him one of the best defensive forwards in the league last season, opponents getting 0.22 fewer expected goals per 60 with him out there, but this year Ottawa's share of the chances is almost four points worse with him on than off. He also has 65 hits, a lot for a center. Watch whether the two-way game catches up to the scoring.
